family_title_en: Complete the sentence with the correct sight word

stages.ix_title: Complete the sentence with the correct sight word

prompt.en: Which sight word completes the sentence?
prompt.ko: 문장을 완성하는 자주 쓰는 단어는 무엇인가요?

what_to_do.en: Tap the word that fits the sentence.

stages.choice_rule: Three lowercase whole-word choices. Exactly one choice fills the hyphen blank and makes a correct Grade 2 sentence. Every stem word and every choice comes from the roots word list or allowed_extra_words, plus <NAME>. Vary answer_index. Tier 1 distractors are obvious same-letter mismatches. Tier 2 distractors are other sight words that share spelling. Tier 3 distractors are homophones or irregular near misses.

gold_items.stem: <NAME> and I - the dog at home.
We stay inside - the rain is cold.
The kids took - books home after school.
The cat has - in the box all day.

roots: Use exactly three choices: one correct sight word and two real words that do not complete the sentence.
Never allow two choices that both make a correct sentence. One right answer only.
Every choice is a whole word in classroom spelling. Do not use list typos such as becaus, thier, theyre, or wuz.
Tier 1 wrong choices share the first letter but are easy to reject, such as gold or good for go.
Tier 2 wrong choices are other sight words with shared letters, such as where or wear for were.
Tier 3 wrong choices are homophones or irregular near misses, such as there for their or bean for been.
Mark the missing word with one hyphen between spaces. Do not use underscores, slashes, or sound symbols.
Use only roots list words, allowed extra words, and <NAME>. No brands and no real child names.
Keep sentences in school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather. Write original sentences, not copied question text.
Set explain_key to lookalike, were_wear, saw_past, reason_word, whose_word, been_form, homophone, irregular, or fits.

tier_rules.1: Short stems of four to six words. The sight word is common, and the two distractors share its first letter but cannot fit.
tier_rules.2: Stems of five to eight words about home, pets, play, or weather. Distractors are other sight words that look close but break the grammar.
tier_rules.3: Longer stems up to ten words. Use near misses such as their and there, been and bean, were and where, or to, too, and two. Only one choice may fit.

lookalike.en: These words look alike. Read the sentence and tap the one that fits.
lookalike.ko: 이 단어들은 모양이 비슷합니다. 문장을 읽고 맞는 단어를 누르세요.

were_wear.en: Were tells about the past. Where is a place. Wear means put on.
were_wear.ko: Were는 과거를 말합니다. Where는 장소이고 Wear는 입는다는 뜻입니다.

saw_past.en: Saw means we looked. Was tells a state. Say means to speak.
saw_past.ko: Saw는 보았다는 뜻입니다. Was는 상태이고 Say는 말하다는 뜻입니다.

reason_word.en: Because tells why. Become and between do not give a reason.
reason_word.ko: Because는 이유를 말합니다. Become과 between은 이유가 아닙니다.

whose_word.en: Their tells whose it is. There and where are about a place.
whose_word.ko: Their는 누구의 것인지 나타냅니다. There와 where는 장소입니다.

been_form.en: Been goes after has. Bean is a food. Begin means to start.
been_form.ko: Been은 has 뒤에 옵니다. Bean은 음식이고 Begin은 시작입니다.

homophone.en: These words sound almost the same. Meanings differ, so tap the one that fits.
homophone.ko: 이 단어들은 소리가 거의 같습니다. 뜻이 다르니 맞는 단어를 누르세요.

irregular.en: This sight word breaks the usual spelling. Tap the form that fits the sentence.
irregular.ko: 이 단어는 보통 철자 규칙과 다릅니다. 문장에 맞는 형태를 누르세요.

fits.en: Only one word completes the sentence. The other words do not fit.
fits.ko: 한 단어만 문장을 완성합니다. 다른 단어는 맞지 않습니다.
